questions.question_text: Explain the different types of conditional statements in C.

answer_key.model_answer: Conditional statements include: if executes a block when a condition is true; if-else provides two choices; else-if ladder checks multiple conditions from top to bottom; nested if places one if inside another; switch selects one block based on an expression value.
answer_key.marking_rubric: Award 1 mark for each of the five correctly explained types and 1 mark for a clear introduction.
answer_key.important_keywords: if, if-else, else-if ladder, nested if, switch

questions.question_text: Explain the if statement with its syntax and example.

answer_key.model_answer: The if statement executes a block when the condition is true. Syntax: if (condition) { statement; } Example: if (age >= 18) { printf("Adult"); }
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark definition; 2 marks syntax; 2 marks example; 1 mark explanation of true condition.
answer_key.important_keywords: if, condition, true, syntax, example

questions.question_text: Explain the if-else statement with syntax and an example.

answer_key.model_answer: The if-else statement provides two choices. If the condition is true, the if block executes; otherwise, the else block executes. Example: if (n % 2 == 0) { printf("Even"); } else { printf("Odd"); }
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark definition; 2 marks structure; 2 marks example; 1 mark explaining both outcomes.
answer_key.important_keywords: if-else, two choices, true, false, if block, else block

questions.question_text: Explain the else-if ladder with its working and syntax.

answer_key.model_answer: The else-if ladder checks multiple conditions from top to bottom. When a true condition is found, its block executes. Structure: if (condition1) { statement1; } else if (condition2) { statement2; } else if (condition3) { statement3; } else { statement4; }
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks purpose and working; 2 marks checking order; 2 marks correct structure.
answer_key.important_keywords: multiple conditions, top to bottom, if, else if, else

questions.question_text: Explain the nested if statement with its syntax.

answer_key.model_answer: When one if statement is placed inside another if statement, it is called a nested if. The inner if is written inside the outer if block. Structure: if (condition1) { if (condition2) { statement; } }
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition; 2 marks outer and inner if explanation; 2 marks structure.
answer_key.important_keywords: nested if, one if inside another, outer if, inner if

questions.question_text: Explain the switch statement with syntax and example.

answer_key.model_answer: The switch statement selects one block from multiple choices based on an expression value. It uses case labels and may include default. Example: int choice = 2; switch (choice) { case 1: printf("One"); break; case 2: printf("Two"); break; default: printf("Invalid choice"); }
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark definition; 2 marks structure; 2 marks example; 1 mark explaining case, break or default.
answer_key.important_keywords: switch, expression, case, break, default

questions.question_text: Explain the while loop with syntax and example.

answer_key.model_answer: The while loop checks the condition before executing statements. Example: int i = 1; while (i <= 5) { printf("%d ", i); i++; } Output: 1 2 3 4 5.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks working; 2 marks syntax/example; 1 mark increment; 1 mark output.
answer_key.important_keywords: while loop, condition before body, i <= 5, i++, output

questions.question_text: Explain the do-while loop with syntax and example.

answer_key.model_answer: The do-while loop executes statements first and checks the condition after the body. Therefore, it executes at least once. Example: int i = 1; do { printf("%d ", i); i++; } while (i <= 5); Output: 1 2 3 4 5.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks working; 1 mark at-least-once property; 2 marks example; 1 mark output.
answer_key.important_keywords: do-while, body first, condition after body, at least once

questions.question_text: Explain the for loop with syntax and example.

answer_key.model_answer: The for loop is commonly used when the number of repetitions is known. Syntax: for (initialization; condition; increment/decrement) { statements; } Example: for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { printf("%d ", i); }
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark use; 2 marks syntax and parts; 2 marks example; 1 mark explanation.
answer_key.important_keywords: for loop, known repetitions, initialization, condition, increment/decrement

questions.question_text: Differentiate between while, do-while and for loops.

answer_key.model_answer: The while loop checks the condition before its body. The do-while loop checks after its body and executes at least once. The for loop has initialization, condition and increment/decrement in its header and is commonly used when repetitions are known.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks for each loop's correct working and distinction.
answer_key.important_keywords: while, before body, do-while, after body, for, initialization, condition, increment

questions.question_text: Explain the break statement with an example and output.

answer_key.model_answer: The break statement immediately terminates a loop and control moves to the statement following it. Example: for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i == 3) break; printf("%d ", i); } Output: 1 2.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition/effect; 2 marks example; 1 mark termination at i==3; 1 mark output.
answer_key.important_keywords: break, immediately terminate, statement following loop, output 1 2

questions.question_text: Explain the continue statement with an example and output.

answer_key.model_answer: The continue statement skips the remaining statements of the current iteration and starts the next iteration. Example: for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i == 3) continue; printf("%d ", i); } Output: 1 2 4 5.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition; 2 marks example; 1 mark skipped iteration; 1 mark output.
answer_key.important_keywords: continue, skips remaining statements, next iteration, output 1 2 4 5

questions.question_text: Explain the goto statement with an example.

answer_key.model_answer: The goto statement transfers control to a labeled statement within the same function. Example: int i = 1; start: printf("%d ", i); i++; if (i <= 5) goto start; Output: 1 2 3 4 5.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition; 2 marks label and transfer; 1 mark example; 1 mark output.
answer_key.important_keywords: goto, labeled statement, same function, start label

questions.question_text: Explain the different loop control statements in C.

answer_key.model_answer: The notes describe break, continue and goto. break immediately terminates a loop. continue skips the remaining statements of the current iteration and starts the next iteration. goto transfers control to a labeled statement within the same function.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks for each correctly explained statement.
answer_key.important_keywords: break, continue, goto, terminate, skip iteration, labeled statement

questions.question_text: What is an infinite loop? Explain its examples in C.

answer_key.model_answer: An infinite loop continues indefinitely because its condition never becomes false. Examples: while (1) { printf("Hello\n"); } and for (;;) { printf("Hello\n"); }. An incorrect condition can also cause one, such as int i=1; while (i<=5) { printf("%d ",i); } when i is not updated.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition/reason; 1.5 marks each for two examples; 1 mark for incorrect-condition example.
answer_key.important_keywords: infinite loop, condition never false, while (1), for (;;), variable not updated

questions.question_text: Define an array and explain its important features.

answer_key.model_answer: An array is a collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations and identified by a single name. Elements are accessed using an index starting from 0. Features include same data type, fixed size, contiguous memory, index-based access, fast access and storing multiple values.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition; up to 4 marks for correctly explaining features.
answer_key.important_keywords: same data type, contiguous memory, single name, index starts at 0, fixed size, fast access

questions.question_text: Explain a one-dimensional array with syntax and example.

answer_key.model_answer: A one-dimensional array has elements arranged in a single sequence and requires one index. Syntax: data_type array_name[size]; Example: int marks[5] = {80, 75, 90, 85, 70};
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition/one index; 1 mark syntax; 2 marks example; 1 mark index access.
answer_key.important_keywords: one-dimensional, single sequence, one index, syntax, marks[5]

questions.question_text: Explain a two-dimensional array with syntax and example.

answer_key.model_answer: A two-dimensional array contains rows and columns and requires two indices. It is commonly used for a matrix or table. Syntax: data_type array_name[rows][columns]; Example: int matrix[2][3] = {{1,2,3},{4,5,6}}; matrix[1][2] is 6.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition/two indices; 1 mark syntax; 2 marks example; 1 mark element access.
answer_key.important_keywords: two-dimensional, rows, columns, two indices, matrix, table

questions.question_text: Explain a multidimensional array with syntax and example.

answer_key.model_answer: An array having more than two dimensions is called a multidimensional array. It is used when data needs to be organized in more than two dimensions. Syntax: data_type array_name[size1][size2][size3]; Example: int a[2][3][4];
answer_key.marking_rubric: 2 marks definition/use; 2 marks syntax; 2 marks example.
answer_key.important_keywords: multidimensional, more than two dimensions, syntax, int a[2][3][4]

questions.question_text: What is a string in C? Explain any four predefined string functions.

answer_key.model_answer: A string in C is a sequence of characters terminated by '\0'. Functions in string.h include strlen() to find length excluding '\0'; strcpy() to copy a string; strcat() to append one string to another; strcmp() to compare strings, returning 0 if equal, negative if first is less, positive if first is greater.
answer_key.marking_rubric: 1 mark string definition; 1 mark null character/header; 1 mark for each of four functions.
answer_key.important_keywords: string, null character, string.h, strlen, strcpy, strcat, strcmp
